- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.67) over recent days, model tends to overestimate; reduce forecast slightly, especially after spikes.
- When sentiment is negative (≤0.33) or volatile, model often underestimates; increase forecast moderately, especially in early horizon.
- Model frequently overshoots after sharp upward spikes in price; apply a 1–2 day lag correction or dampen peak forecasts.
- Mean reversion bias: if forecast is >10% above recent 5-day average, reduce by 5–10% unless sentiment strongly supports.
- Horizon-specific: 30-day forecasts often overreact to short-term sentiment; cap forecast at 1.5x recent 10-day average unless sentiment is strongly bullish.
- If sentiment history shows alternating bullish/bearish cycles, model tends to misalign with cycle phase; adjust forecast to match sentiment trend direction.
